newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar and Bosnia in gas and oil refinery talks.
newsitem.headline: Qatar and Bosnia in gas and oil refinery talks.

text.p: Bosnia is discussing a deal to buy between 1. 5 and 2.5 million tonnes a year of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Qatar, a Bosnian official was quoted as saying on Monday.

"We will be buying between 1.5 and 2.5 million tonnes of LNG from Qatar to generate power to rebuild our war-torn economy urgently," Ebid Bukvic, general manager of Energoinvest, Bosnia's largest energy firm, told a Qatari newspaper.
Energoinvest has also offered Qatar a stake in a new oil refinery in return for financial help in repairing its war-damaged refinery at Sarajevo.

"We...suggested Qatar can invest in setting up a new refinery or buy shares in the proposed one or help repair the (existing) Sarajevo refinery," Energoinvest deputy general manager Mensur Causevic told the paper.
The gas supply deal was likely to be finalised after a receiving terminal, a regasification plant and pipeline network had been set up in Bosnia, he said.
Qatari oil officials have said that Bosnia was looking for gas supplies from the year 2005.

"The European Commission, assisted by the U.S., has set up an international organisation to oversee the implementation of a project to link 12 eastern European nations, including Bosnia, into a common pipeline grid", he said.
"We are planning to build the infrastructure to receive the Qatari LNG at Ploce or Neum, the southern port cities of Bosnia," said the Bosnian ambassador to Qatar, Nusret Cancar.
Cancar said diversification of energy supplies was vital as the existing pipeline that supplies Russian gas to Bosnia from Russia crossed Serbian territory.
Bosnia imports around 50 million cubic metres a day of gas from Russian gas giant Gazprom.
"Eastern Europe is politically not yet stable and so we have decided to buy gas from other sources as well", he said, adding his country has received offers from Algeria and Qatar.
